titulo: Your piece: a 15 s opening in 16:9 and 9:16, rendered and checked
lead: Time to put it all together into a piece you actually use: a 15 s opening with your DESIGN.md, in the two formats social networks ask for. The 9:16 doesn't come from the 16:9 through a render option: it's another composition that reuses the CSS and the choreography. In this lesson you deliver both, checked by the kit, and build the plan with dates.
objetivo: deliver a 15 s opening in 16:9 and 9:16, with the DESIGN.md, checked by the kit in both formats.

blocos.rot: Terminal · brand, check, two renders and conferir
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/formacao-cinema-ia-motion-v72/kit
export HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 NO_COLOR=1
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-motion/a8; rm -rf "$E"; mkdir -p "$E"
cp -r "$K/exemplos/a8-abertura" "$E/abertura"; cd "$E/abertura"
python3 "$K/conferir-design.py" DESIGN.md abertura.css; echo "saída: $?"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 check 2>&1 | grep -E "Check passed|✗"
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render --quality draft --workers 2 --quiet --output renders/abertura-16x9.mp4 > render-16x9.log 2>&1
npx -y hyperframes@0.8.176 render -c formatos/vertical.html --quality draft --workers 2 --quiet --output renders/abertura-9x16.mp4 > render-9x16.log 2>&1
python3 "$K/conferir.py" renders/abertura-16x9.mp4 15 1920x1080; echo "saída: $?"
python3 "$K/conferir.py" renders/abertura-9x16.mp4 15 1080x1920; echo "saída: $?"

The 9:16 render uses -c formatos/vertical.html. vertical.html is index.html with the root at 1080×1920, the vertical class, and the paths ../abertura.css and ../abertura.js.

✗  Output resolution incompatible

   outputResolution portrait (1080×1920) does not match the aspect ratio of the composition (1920×1080). The composition is landscape, so use --resolution landscape instead.

The --resolution option changes the resolution within the same aspect ratio (for example, 4K). Going from 16:9 to 9:16 means changing the framing: a different composition.

On the first render, the 9:16 broke the title into "Motion por" / "código": failure 2 from lesson 3. The fix was to tie the last two words together with   in the HTML ("por código"). It only showed up by looking at the frames.

txt.titulo: Plan — Motion by code with an agent
txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: How do you get the 9:16 out of the same opening?
opcoes: Rotate the 16:9 MP4 in FFmpeg and adjust the scale.
Another 1080×1920 composition with the same CSS.
Crop the sides of the 16:9 in a video editor.
perguntas.explica: 0.8.176 refuses --resolution portrait on a landscape composition. Rotating or cropping loses text and framing. Another composition with the same style is the path the render accepts.

perguntas.p: Why does the choreography read the root's width (data-width)?
opcoes: Because GSAP only accepts distances in absolute pixels.
So the head can run the whole track in both formats.
Because lint requires reading data-width in every composition.
So the vertical video ends up shorter than the horizontal one.
perguntas.explica: The track takes up 80% of the width; the distance changes between 1920 and 1080 px. Reading the root's measure lets one choreography serve both.

perguntas.p: The 9:16 render failed after the 16:9 was done. What do you redo?
opcoes: Only the 9:16 render, and check it.
Both renders together, to save time.
perguntas.explica: What is done and checked is not redone. And rendering both together on a busy machine is how the second one fails from memory.

itens.texto: Two compositions, one style: shared CSS and choreography.
DESIGN.md checked, check passing, and the checker run on both MP4s.
One render at a time; redo only what failed.
